65 y/o woman establishing care. Turned 65 in May, new to Medicare Part B (Aetna supplement, Plan F); today doubles as her Welcome to Medicare visit. Prior office records reviewed before the visit (summary in chart 9/4).

HPI / active issues
1. Hypertension: on HCTZ 25 mg every morning for years, no side effects she can name. No home cuff. No headaches, chest pain, dyspnea or ankle swelling.
2. Knees: both knees stiff first thing in the morning, loosens up within a few minutes of walking. No swelling, no locking, no pain at rest. Takes nothing for it and does not want anything.

PMH: HTN; mild bilateral knee OA; lactose intolerance (has avoided dairy most of her life, so her calcium intake has been low for a long time).
PSH: left cataract extraction with IOL (does not remember the year). No other surgery.
OB/GYN: menopause at 45. Never on hormone therapy. Co-tests normal through 2017, the last at 64.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mother with hypertension, broke her hip at 82 (osteoporosis). Father with atrial fibrillation and hypertension. Sister has Graves disease. Maternal grandmother had rheumatoid arthritis. No one with kidney stones that she knows of.
Social: lives in South Hadley on her own. Administrative consultant, remote, starting to scale back toward retirement. Never smoked. Wine socially, a glass or two most weeks, sometimes nothing for weeks at a time. Walks most days.

ROS: negative except knees as above. No palpitations, weight change, heat or cold intolerance, bowel change.

Exam
Vitals per flowsheet. Slim, well appearing. Eyes: left pseudophakic, right lens clear to penlight. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged, no nodules. Heart regular rate and rhythm, S1 S2 normal, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Knees: mild crepitus both sides, no effusion, full range. No edema. Gait normal, gets up from the chair without using her arms.

Welcome to Medicare elements
- Vision: reads the wall chart without difficulty with glasses. Hearing: passes whisper test both sides.
- Depression screen PHQ-2: 0. Alcohol (AUDIT-C): 2.
- Functional status: independent in all ADLs and IADLs. Home safety reviewed: no throw rugs, has grab bar in the shower. No falls in the past year.
- Advance directive: she has not done one; information handout given, will think about naming a health care proxy.

Assessment / plan
1. HTN, controlled on HCTZ 25. Continue. BMP today.
2. Knee OA, mild. Keep walking. Nothing else wanted.
3. Prevention:
   - Colon: colonoscopy 2016 normal, next due 2026.
   - Breast: mammogram ordered.
   - Cervical: stopping screening now that she is 65 with a run of normal co-tests; explained.
   - Bone density: with early menopause, a mother with a hip fracture and years of low calcium intake she is a good candidate for a DXA. Offered it. She would rather not do it right now ("I'll think about it next year"). Will revisit at her wellness visit.
   - Lipids, one-time HCV and HIV screening today.
   - Vaccines: flu shot and Prevnar 13 when the flu vaccine arrives next month (nurse visit). Shingrix discussed, she will check pharmacy coverage. Unsure of last tetanus booster; Tdap next visit.
4. Return in 6 months for BP, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Office Visit - palpitations, weight loss
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: "my heart races and I'm losing weight without trying."

HPI: 68 y/o with HTN on HCTZ booked this herself. Since around the start of the year she has noticed her heart pounding or fluttering, mostly when sitting quietly in the evening, lasting minutes to longer, no fainting. Feels warm when others are comfortable, sleeps with the window open. Eating more than usual, yet clothes are looser. Bowels moving more often than they used to, formed, not diarrhea. No chest pain, no shortness of breath at rest. No neck pain. No new medicines or supplements, no iodine contrast, no biotin.
Sister has Graves disease and she wondered about that herself.

Weight today 55 kg; 58 kg at her wellness visit last September.

Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: pulse 104 and regular at rooming, 98 on the ECG a few minutes later. Afebrile. Thin, comfortable. Eyes: no proptosis, no lid lag that I can appreciate. Neck nontender. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear.

ECG in office: sinus rhythm 98, no other abnormality.

Assessment: her symptoms strongly suggest hyperthyroidism, Graves likely given family history. Unintentional weight loss of 3 kg.
Plan:
- TSH now; I'll call with the result. If suppressed, urgent endocrinology referral.
- Return/ED precautions reviewed: chest pain, fainting, heart rate that stays very fast or irregular, shortness of breath.
- Bone health: overactive thyroid adds to her bone risk on top of early menopause, mother's hip fracture and years of little dietary calcium. Raised the DXA again and this time she agrees. Ordered.

documents.title: Your bone density result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Sandra,

Your bone density scan shows osteoporosis: T-score -2.8 at the lower spine and -2.7 at the hip (anything at or below -2.5 is in that range). Early menopause, your mother's history and a lifetime with little dairy all play a part, and the overactive thyroid likely adds to it.

- Vitamin D3 2000 units once a day.

There are prescription medicines that lower fracture risk, and I'd like to go over them with you. No rush this week with the thyroid appointment coming up.

Your PCP

ENDOCRINOLOGY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Visit date: 07/20/2021
Referred by: primary care, for suppressed TSH

Thank you for sending Ms. Walsh, a 68-year-old woman with hypertension and newly found osteoporosis.

History: For roughly half a year she has had episodes of a racing heartbeat, intolerance of warm rooms, and a weight drop despite eating more. Bowel movements have become more frequent though not loose. No eye irritation, double vision or neck pain. No recent iodine load, no amiodarone, no biotin.

Past history: hypertension; mild bilateral knee osteoarthritis; osteoporosis on DXA 7/13/21 (L1-L4 -2.8, femoral neck -2.7); menopause at 45, no HRT; lactose intolerance. Surgery: left cataract with IOL.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg TID with meals; cholecalciferol 2000 units daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: sister with Graves disease; father with atrial fibrillation and hypertension; mother with hypertension and osteoporotic hip fracture at 82; maternal grandmother with rheumatoid arthritis.
Social: never smoker; wine socially, 1-2 glasses a week, with periods of none. Semi-retired, works from home.

Exam: HR 102, BP 138/86, weight 55 kg. Fine tremor with arms outstretched. Skin warm and moist. Thyroid diffusely enlarged, smooth, not tender, no nodules, no bruit. No proptosis or lid retraction. Heart irregularly irregular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

Data:
TSH <0.01 mIU/L (0.4-4.0)
Free T4 3.2 ng/dL (0.8-1.8)
Calcium 10.2 mg/dL (8.5-10.2)
Alkaline phosphatase 150 U/L (30-120)
Transaminases, bilirubin, albumin normal; CBC normal (baseline before antithyroid drug).
ECG today: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Her ECG at your office on 7/6 was sinus.

Assessment:
1. Graves disease: overt hyperthyroidism with a diffuse nontender goiter, fine tremor and a sister with the same diagnosis. The alkaline phosphatase and high-normal calcium fit increased bone turnover from thyrotoxicosis.
2. Atrial fibrillation with RVR, paroxysmal, driven by thyrotoxicosis.
3. Osteoporosis, with thyrotoxicosis a contributor.

Plan:
- Methimazole 10 mg daily. Reviewed agranulocytosis warning (stop and call for fever or sore throat) and liver symptoms. Baseline CBC and liver tests done today.
- Metoprolol tartrate 25 mg twice daily for rate and symptom control.
- Repeat free T4 and TSH with ECG at follow-up in about 8 weeks.
- Continue HCTZ, calcium and vitamin D as prescribed by you.

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

documents.body:
Here to talk through bone protection, about three months after her first endocrinology visit for Graves.

S: Nothing acute. Feels well. Admits she's been less active the last few years as her consulting work tapered off. No pain at rest. Stiff when she first gets out of bed, and thinks she walks a bit slower than she used to. Knees: the same mild arthritis, nothing new. Never fallen, never broken a bone. ROS negative for weakness, numbness and any recent weight change (weight steady since summer). Palpitations gone off metoprolol.

Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily (her only BP medicine); methimazole 10 mg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg TID with meals; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
NKDA. Never smoker, occasional glass of wine.

O: Vitals normal (flowsheet). Well appearing. Spine without tenderness. Strength 5/5 in hips and legs, rises from chair without hands. Gait steady, normal tandem walk. Knees mild crepitus, no effusion.

DXA 7/13/21 reviewed with her: L1-L4 T -2.8, femoral neck T -2.7.

A/P: Osteoporosis, postmenopausal, risk factors early menopause, maternal hip fracture, long low calcium intake, recent thyrotoxicosis.
We went through options: weekly alendronate, a yearly zoledronic acid infusion, and denosumab injections every 6 months, with how much each lowers fracture risk and the side effects she has read about (jaw osteonecrosis, unusual thigh fractures, stomach upset). She would rather not take a bone drug now - the side effects worry her and she wants to give the non-drug approach a fair try first, and let the thyroid settle. Her choice; she knows she can revisit any time.
- Continue calcium carbonate 600 mg TID and D3 2000 units.
- Weight-bearing exercise: daily brisk walking, add simple balance and leg-strength work (handout).
- Fall prevention at home: lighting on stairs, nonslip mat, shoes with grip outdoors.
- Getting the Graves under control will help her bones.
HTN on HCTZ controlled. Next visit March.

69 y/o with osteoporosis, Graves (euthyroid on methimazole), HTN, back about a year after our bone-health talk.

S: Over the past year she has felt steadily more tired, and has a mild ache across the middle of her back. She puts both down to getting older and to hunching over the laptop at her kitchen-table desk. No focal weakness, no pins and needles, no real joint pain beyond the usual knee stiffness. Still walks every day. She has the sense she's gotten shorter and her trousers sit differently at the waist.
No fever, night sweats, weight loss, change in bowels or bladder. No palpitations or heat intolerance.
Diet: still avoids dairy - lactose intolerance - so her calcium is from the tablets.
Menopause at 45, never on HRT.
Meds: HCTZ 25 daily; methimazole 10 daily; calcium carbonate 600 TID; D3 2000 units daily. NKDA.

O: BP 132/78, P 76, SpO2 98%. Wt 54 kg, Ht 160 cm, BMI 21.1.
Her height in the 2017 records from her prior practice was 163 cm, and our own measurements ran 162.5 to 163.9 cm through 2021.
Mild thoracic kyphosis. No midline spinal tenderness to percussion. Paraspinals soft.
Neuro: strength 5/5 throughout, reflexes symmetric, sensation intact to light touch, gait normal, Romberg negative.
Heart RRR, lungs clear, abdomen soft.

A/P:
1. Fatigue, gradual - check CBC, BMP with calcium, TSH and free T4.
2. Mid-back discomfort with mild thoracic kyphosis and 3 cm loss of height, in a woman with osteoporosis. Neuro exam normal. Posture changes at her workstation (laptop riser, chair with lumbar support), keep walking daily, back extension exercises (handout, shown in the room).

Will message results.

OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 09/27/2023
Preoperative / postoperative diagnosis: right anterior glenohumeral fracture-dislocation, surgical neck of humerus.
Procedure: open reduction of the glenohumeral dislocation; ORIF, right proximal humerus, locking plate.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Ms. Walsh came in on 11/10/2023 for routine follow-up, this time with questions of her own about her bones. Osteoporosis was found on her first DXA in July 2021, and in September she fractured the right humeral surgical neck (with an anterior dislocation) in a fall from standing, fixed surgically on 9/27. She wanted to understand what the fracture says about her bones and whether she should change how she eats.

Since the fracture she has deliberately added dairy and more green vegetables; despite her lactose intolerance she is tolerating the amounts she takes. She lives on her own and walks every day. She has no back pain, no joint pain and no difficulty walking. Nothing in her history suggests a malignancy, malabsorption or other chronic illness. Menopause at 45, never on hormone therapy. Screening is current: the 2016 colonoscopy and her most recent mammogram were both clear.

Medications: methimazole 10 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg three times daily; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: none known.
Family history: mother with an osteoporotic hip fracture at 82; sister with Graves disease. No family history of kidney stones.

Exam: vital signs normal. Thin, well-appearing woman. Spine without tenderness or deformity. Gait steady. Neurological examination normal. Thyroid not enlarged.

DXA 10/24/2023: L1-L4 T-score -2.7, left femoral neck -2.9.
Labs today: calcium, creatinine, albumin, alkaline phosphatase, liver enzymes, TSH, free T4 and 25-hydroxyvitamin D all within normal limits. No secondary cause of bone loss is evident, and none of these results was expected to be abnormal in her case.

Assessment: postmenopausal osteoporosis with a fragility fracture; Graves disease, euthyroid on methimazole 10 mg.
Discussion: I explained that a fracture after a fall from standing, together with her T-scores, puts her at high risk of another fracture over the next few years, and that the hip number has slipped since 2021. We reviewed the treatment choices again - an oral or intravenous bisphosphonate, denosumab, and the bone-building injectables. She listened carefully and decided against any bone medication for now; she remains worried about side effects. Dairy in the amounts she is having is fine and gives her calcium from food. Continue calcium carbonate and vitamin D3, weight-bearing activity and fall precautions.
Plan: continue methimazole 10 mg; TSH/free T4 every 6 months at your lab; see her again in a year.

Endocrinology

Chief complaint: burning skin pain and dark patches on the lower abdomen and thighs.

Yesterday she developed burning pain in the skin of the lower abdomen and upper thighs, and the areas have darkened and spread quickly since. No fever. EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE - 01/10/2026

Chief complaint: confusion, constipation and weakness for two weeks.

HPI: 72-year-old woman with osteoporosis, hypertension, Graves disease and paroxysmal AF on warfarin, brought in by her sister. Over the past two weeks she has been muddled - losing track of conversations, forgetting what she went into a room for - with constipation and generalized weakness. No fever, falls, head injury, headache, vomiting or urinary symptoms.
Wanting to strengthen her bones, she has been taking extra calcium carbonate tablets she buys over the counter on top of her usual 600 mg three times a day, and drinking milk every day; she thinks this started around the fall but cannot say how many extra tablets a day. She also takes her prescribed thiazide diuretic for blood pressure.

Medications (patient and sister):
- hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily
- calcium carbonate 600 mg three times daily, plus additional OTC calcium carbonate tablets (amount unknown)
- cholecalciferol 2000 units daily
- methimazole 10 mg daily
- warfarin 5 mg daily
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 88. Lethargic but rousable. No focal neurological deficit. Abdomen soft, non-tender, non-distended. No bruising or bleeding.

Labs: calcium 12.5 mg/dL (8.5-10.2); creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (0.6-1.1); BUN 35 mg/dL (7-20); serum bicarbonate elevated.
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.52, HCO3 32 mEq/L, PaCO2 42 mmHg - metabolic alkalosis.
Urinalysis normal. CBC unremarkable. INR 2.9, within her warfarin goal of 2-3.

Assessment: milk-alkali syndrome - hypercalcemia, metabolic alkalosis and reduced kidney function from heavy calcium carbonate and milk intake, with a thiazide reducing urinary calcium excretion.
Plan: IV normal saline started. Hold calcium carbonate and hydrochlorothiazide. PTH sent. Admit to medicine.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission 01/10/2026 - Discharge 01/13/2026
Principal diagnosis: milk-alkali syndrome.

Course: admitted from the ED with two weeks of confusion, constipation and weakness after months of extra over-the-counter calcium carbonate and daily milk on top of her prescribed calcium and hydrochlorothiazide. Calcium 12.5, creatinine 2.1, BUN 35, metabolic alkalosis on blood gas. Treated with IV normal saline. Calcium carbonate and hydrochlorothiazide stopped. PTH 9 pg/mL (15-65), appropriately suppressed, supporting a non-PTH cause. Calcium and creatinine improved each day. Confusion cleared by hospital day 2 and she was back to her usual self. Bowels moving before discharge.
Discharge labs: calcium 9.9 mg/dL, creatinine 1.4 mg/dL.
Warfarin and methimazole continued throughout; INR stayed within her 2-3 warfarin goal.

Discharge medications:
- STOPPED calcium carbonate (all, including OTC)
- STOPPED hydrochlorothiazide
- CONTINUE cholecalciferol 2000 units daily
- CONTINUE methimazole 10 mg daily
- CONTINUE warfarin 5 mg daily
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within a week - recheck calcium and creatinine, and blood pressure off the thiazide; an alternative antihypertensive may be needed. Avoid calcium supplements; keep milk and dairy to ordinary amounts.

TCM visit. ED note and discharge summary reviewed.

Admitted 1/10-1/13 with milk-alkali syndrome: calcium 12.5, creatinine 2.1, BUN 35, metabolic alkalosis, PTH suppressed at 9. She had been taking extra OTC calcium carbonate on top of her 600 mg TID plus daily milk since around the fall, while on HCTZ. Treated with saline; calcium carbonate and HCTZ stopped. Discharge calcium 9.9, creatinine 1.4.

Today: thinking is clear - she and I had a normal, detailed conversation, and she recalls the hospital stay. Bowels back to normal. Energy returning. No headache.
She was upset with herself; she had read that more calcium would make her bones stronger after the fracture.

Meds now: warfarin 5 mg (anticoag clinic); methimazole 10 mg; vitamin D3 2000 units. No calcium tablets. HCTZ stopped.

Exam: BP 148/88 off HCTZ. Weight 55 kg. Alert, oriented, fluent. Mucous membranes moist. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

Labs today (resulted this afternoon): calcium 9.6, creatinine 1.1 - both continuing to improve.

A/P:
1. Milk-alkali syndrome, resolving. Stop ALL calcium tablets - prescribed and OTC. Milk and dairy fine in ordinary amounts (a serving or two a day), no more "extra for the bones." Continue vitamin D3 2000 units. Repeat BMP in a few weeks.
2. HTN, BP up off the thiazide. Not restarting HCTZ. Sent a question to her cardiologist about the best replacement given her AF and warfarin; will start something once I hear back. Home BP log in the meantime.
3. Osteoporosis: without calcium tablets she'll rely on dietary calcium. Discussed.
